name: ACP
description: Any Agent Client Protocol agent (Zed's ACP: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio), mapped onto the runner protocol. Presets: Google's Gemini CLI (`gemini --experimental-acp`), handshake verified — the runner fetches the pinned @google/gemini-cli bundle on first boot, since nothing stages it into the colony image; and xAI's Grok Build (`grok agent stdio`), handshake verified against grok 1.0.34 but not yet driven through a turn with a real XAI_API_KEY — nothing stages the grok binary either. Other ACP agents run through a custom command. Questions ride session/request_permission, file paths resolve inside the workspace, and terminal commands are only started with a workspace cwd.

requires.image: glibc + node >= 20; the gemini preset needs no gemini on PATH (the runner fetches the pinned @google/gemini-cli bundle on first boot), while the grok preset still needs the grok binary, which nothing stages

session_resume.description: The gemini preset keeps its sessions under ~/.gemini and the runner reloads one with session/load, so a colony waiting on the user can be suspended (its microVM stopped) and continued with the conversation intact; a custom agent resumes only if it keeps its sessions there too.

agent.title: ACP agent
agent.description: Which ACP agent to launch. `gemini` is the verified one: Google's Gemini CLI in its ACP mode (`gemini --experimental-acp`), authenticated with the GEMINI_API_KEY secret for generativelanguage.googleapis.com. `grok` is xAI's Grok Build in its ACP mode (`grok agent stdio`), authenticated with the XAI_API_KEY secret for api.x.ai: verified at the handshake (initialize, session/new with model selection) against grok 1.0.34, but a turn with a real XAI_API_KEY has not been run. `custom` launches any other ACP agent through the command below — declare its API hosts and credential in your deployment, since this manifest only declares Gemini's and grok's.

command.title: Custom command
command.description: Used when the ACP agent is `custom`: the full command line including arguments, e.g. `node /opt/acp-agent/main.js --stdio`. Quote spans with single or double quotes to keep arguments with spaces whole.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model id applied with session/set_model after session/new, when the agent advertises model selection there (the gemini and grok presets do). An agent that advertises no models cannot select one: it keeps its own default and the runner logs a warning. Switching the model on a running colony works the same way.

exec_policy.title: Exec policy
exec_policy.description: JSON exec policy this install layers over the built-in one: {"rules": [{"id", "decision": "deny"|"ask"|"allow", "reason", "command"|"script"|"touches"|"writes_outside"}]} (see modules/agents/acp/README.md). A matched rule answers session/request_permission for the command tool calls it names: allow approves the call without asking you, deny refuses it, ask becomes a question to you. Layers can only narrow: the built-in deny rules always hold, an org policy (COLONIZER_EXEC_POLICY_ORG) narrows further, and a repository's own .colonizer/exec-policy.json narrows further still. Empty uses the built-in policy alone.
